sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre. 2024 [first version 2017]. Contribution à la classification des langues kru (Niger-Congo). Ms., Institut d'ethnologie, Université de Strasbourg, 74 pp. HAL hal-04390526v4 (Glottolog ref 589953 = 2017 version).
sources.note: Comparative Kru overview; sec. 2.4 (p.7): 'Les systèmes de tons sont à trois (bassa, klao, neyo...) ou quatre registres (grebo, bété, vata...)'. 'Grebo' data are from Glebo sources (Innes, Payne); nothing on stress/accent; nothing specific to Wedebo/Kplebo.

sources.citation: Hasselbring, Sue and Eric Johnson. 2002. A sociolinguistic survey of the Grebo language area of Liberia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-074. 100 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.2.1 'Transcription difficulties' (p.49) gives pan-Grebo remarks only: nine vowels; 'Kru languages are reported to have three or four levels of tone. Grebo orthography distinguishes three tones: high, mid, and low'. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the 100-page report. Contains Wedabo (308-item) and Kplebo (197-item) wordlists and texts; Table 38 groups Kplebo+Wedabo phonetically ([dl]->[tl]).

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.) 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO-BREDA. Page 'Liberia: Grebo (Chlehpo dialect) (Kru)' (Rosetta Project filed under gry).
sources.note: Orthography chart; lists four tones (top, high, mid, low; top and low marked). Nothing on stress. Chlehpo = Chedepo, an E Je / Northern Grebo (nort2810) dialect, so misfiled by Rosetta -- not Barclayville Grebo.
